title: The unusual cluster Terzan
caption: The stellar cluster Terzan 5, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Terzan 5 · constellation Sagittarius · about 20000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble view peers through the thick dust clouds of our galaxy's central bulge to reveal Terzan 5, a stellar cluster with an unusual mix of stars. An international team of astronomers studied that mix and reached a striking conclusion about the cluster's origins.

Their results indicate that Terzan 5 is not an ordinary cluster but one of the original building blocks of the bulge, probably left over from the Milky Way's earliest days. The bulge is the dense, crowded region of stars around the centre of our galaxy, and working out how it was assembled is a key part of understanding the Milky Way's history.

The observations drew on several telescopes: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, the Multi-conjugate Adaptive Optics Demonstrator (MAD) on ESO's Very Large Telescope, and the second-generation Near Infrared Camera at the Keck Telescope. Infrared light helps here, because it passes through dust that blocks much of the visible light from this region.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.33 x 1.63 arcminutes) and distance (20000 light years), the frame spans roughly 19 × 9.5 light-years. Its light set out about 20,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines visible and near-infrared exposures from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys with near-infrared data from Wide Field Camera 3. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye and passes through dust that dims this cluster in visible light.

explore: Terzan 5 lies about 20,000 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Sagittarius. This image combines visible and near-infrared filters from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3.
alt: A dense stellar cluster seen through the dusty central region of the Milky Way.
